course_description:
This course integrates Advanced Humanities first-year students into a cohort to develop formal analysis skills in writing, music, and the visual.

HUMN1201 integrates Advanced Humanities first-year students into a cohort to develop formal analysis skills in writing, music, and the visual. Students will work individually and in groups to analyse primary source documents and develop critical skills. The course will teach you interdisciplinary analysis methods. It will be an interactive experience, applying a combination of problem-based learning, self-directed learning, student presentations, and group activities. HUMN1201 students will also have access to a number of extra-curricular cohort building activities, but these are not compulsory.

course_aims: HUMN1201 aims to provide students with an introduction to formal analysis skills across disciplines in the humanities, emphasising the importance of critical thinking and close reading. Students will work both individually and in groups to analyse primary sources from multiple humanities disciplines, gaining facility with interdisciplinary analysis skills and methods. The course employs a number of teaching methodologies, including self-directed learning, problem-based learning, group activities, and student presentations, to develop critical skills.

learning_outcomes.description: Draw on a range of interdisciplinary skills to analyse works of writing, music, and art.
Demonstrate facility with different forms of formal and contextual analysis through application of analysis skills to written, sonic, and visual objects.
Demonstrate the application of close-reading skills to the interpretation of a primary source.
Demonstrate an understanding of AI-prompting and the advantages and disadvantages of using AI.
Conceptualise the skills pertinent to formal and contextual analysis of primary sources in an interdisciplinary humanities context.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment includes the submission of two pieces of work. Students will be given a passage from one of the primary sources studied. The first piece of work that must be submitted is an AI-generated commentary on the meaning of the set text in which students will demonstrate an understanding of AI prompting (20% of overall grade). The second piece of work is a 1000-word critique written by the student of the AI-generated commentary. This critique must demonstrate the student's close reading of the relevant passage and indicate where the AI-generated commentary has correctly or incorrectly interpreted the set text (80% of the overall grade). assessment_details.title: Final Exam
assessment_details.task_description: The final exam will consist of essay questions based on the course images, lectures, readings and tutorials. Students will select essay questions from a number of questions on the exam paper. All questions will relate to the formal and historical aspects of works of art that have been discussed in class. The essay questions test a student's understanding of the research methodologies employed by Art Historians through their ability to visually analyse the formal and design aspects of works of art and to comprehend the works’ significance in historical context. Sample questions will be provided and discussed in advance during tutorials. learning_activities.topic: Week 1: Introduction to the Course Introduction to the course. Lecturers: Dr Anne Levitsky, Dr David Kearns, and Dr Ben Pollitt. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Week 2: Intention Lecturer: Dr David Kearns. Students will be introduced to the study of authorial intention as elaborated by Quentin Skinner, with a key focus on whether Mary Wollstonecraft can be described as a feminist. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Tutorial 1: Intention Tutor: Dr David Kearns In-class discussion will focus on Mary Wollstonecraft, ‘A Vindication of the Rights of Woman’, in Sylvana Tomaselli, ed., A Vindication of the Rights of Men and a Vindication of the Rights of Woman (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2012 [1792]), 65-294. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 3: Language Lecturer: Dr David Kearns. Students will be introduced to the study of texts as exhibiting languages, as developed by J. G. A. Pocock, with a key focus on whether Edmund Burke inaugurated conservatism. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Tutorial 2: Language Tutor: Dr David Kearns In-class discussion will focus on Edmund Burke, ‘Reflections on the Revolution in France’, in L. G. Mitchell, ed., The Writings and Speeches of Edmund Burke, Volume 8: The French Revolution: 1790-1794 (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1989 [1790]), 53-293 Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 4: Persona Lecturer: Dr David Kearns. Students will be introduced to the study of persona and, in particular, the role of office in early modern England via Conal Condren, with a key focus on the alleged authoritarianism or liberalism of Thomas Hobbes. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Tutorial 3: Persona Tutor: Dr David Kearns In-class discussion will focus on Thomas Hobbes, The Clarendon Editions of the Works of Thomas Hobbes, Volumes 4 and 5: Leviathan: The English and Latin Texts (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2012 [1651]) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 5: Institutions Lecturer: Dr David Kearns. Students will be introduced to the study of institutional vocabularies, following the work of Ian Hunter and David Saunders, with a key focus on the history of free speech and authorship. Learning outcomes: L03, L05
Tutorial 4: Institutions Tutor: Dr David Kearns In-class discussion will focus on Dominus Rex versus Curl (1727) 93 ER 849-51. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 6: Melody, Rhythm, and Meter Lecture on musical analysis, particularly melody, rhythm, and meter. Lecturer: Dr Anne Levitsky. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Tutorial 5: Gilles Binchois, Dueil anguisseus In this tutorial we will analyse Gilles Binchois' Dueil angoisseus , paying particular attention to melody, rhythm, and meter. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 7: Harmony Lecture on musical harmony. Lecturer: Dr Anne Levitsky. Learning outcomes: L03, L05
Tutorial 6: Schumann, Dichterliebe This tutorial will analyse the lieder of Robert Schumann, focusing particularly on harmony. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 8: Musical Form Lecture on musical form and its analysis. Lecturer: Dr Anne Levitsky. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Tutorial 7: Mozart, Eine Kleine Nachtmusik and Beethoven, Symphony No. 5 This tutorial will focus on Mozart's Eine Kleine Nachtmusik , as well as Beethoven's Symphony No. 5, and will combine application of all the musical elements we have encountered in the course thus far. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 9: No Lecture
Tutorial 8: In-Class Presentations You will present your Favorite Song presentations in this tutorial. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Week 10: Visual Arts I: Form and Meaning Lecturer: Dr Ben Pollitt. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L05
Tutorial 9: Visual Arts I: Form and Meaning Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 11: Visual Arts II: Class and Gender Lecturer: Dr Ben Pollitt. Learning outcomes: L03, L05
